The major types of Chinese classical poetry that are generated include two primary categories: SHI and CI. SHI can be further divided into Jueju and Lvshi, while CI consists of 121 major forms known as Cipai. Jueju and Lvshi are the two major forms of SHI, with Jueju being easier for machine generation due to its four-line structure compared to the eight-line structure of Lvshi, and CI being more complex and still in the early stages of research for automatic generation.
Chinese classical poetry can be classified into two primary categories: SHI and CI. true
SHI can be further divided into Jueju and Lvshi. true
CI consists of 121 major forms known as Cipai. true
Jueju is easier for machine generation due to its four-line structure compared to the eight-line structure of Lvshi. true
Research on the automatic generation of CI is just at the very beginning stage. true
The source of the training/testing data is the Chinese Classical Poetry Corpus (CCPC1.0), which consists of 834,902 poems in total.
The source of the training/testing data is the Chinese Classical Poetry Corpus (CCPC1.0). true

The most helpful strategy identified in the study was the entropy algorithm, which was found to build machine learning models quickly and efficiently. Additionally, vote entropy and KL divergence, which are query-by-committee active learning methods, were also helpful for training machine learning ensemble classifiers, although the active learning strategies tested did not work well with deep learning models.
The entropy algorithm is the best way to build machine learning models fast and efficiently. true

Data is collected by using the original and updated VADER (Valence Aware Dictionary and Sentiment Reasoner) to calculate sentiment scores for about 14,000 Nigerian Pidgin tweets. Additionally, three individuals who are familiar with Nigerian Pidgin were involved in labeling the data, and each labeled data point was verified by at least one other person.

The weakness in Hassan et al's evaluation design is that it relies on crowd workers, who may not be professional translators, and thus their assessments may lack the nuance that expert translators could provide. Additionally, the evaluation often omits linguistic context, which can lead to a less favorable judgment of machine translation quality compared to human translations that consider inter-sentential context.
Hassan et al's evaluation design relies on crowd workers instead of professional translators. true
The evaluation omits linguistic context. true
